Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:10:1.hebrew: נותנין לו - שלא יראה כהן את הנגע, דכל כמה דלא חזי ליה כהן ולא מטמא ליה — לא הוי טמא, דבכהן תלא רחמנא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:10:1.english: They grant him - That a priest should not examine the affliction; for as long as a priest does not inspect it and does not declare it impure, it is not impure, for the Merciful One made [it] dependent upon the priest.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:10:2.hebrew: לאיצטליתו - טליתו, אם נולדו בה נגעי בגדים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:10:2.english: To his cloak - His cloak, if leprous marks of garments appeared on it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:11:1.hebrew: מקמייתא טהר ליה - מיד כשנולד זה, ומזה אינו טמא, דנטרינן ליה יומי דחתונה או של רגל לכל אדם. אלא אי ויטהר תנן, סוף סוף לא מהני ליה מידי הא דנטרינן ליה, דאינו טהור מראשונה עד שתתרפא אחרונה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:11:1.english: He has become pure from the first - Immediately when this [new mark] appears; and from this [one] he is not impure, as we wait for him [during] the days of the wedding feast, or [during] a Festival for any person. But if we learned [the reading] veyitaher [“and he shall be pure”], ultimately, the fact that we wait for him does not benefit him at all, for he is not pure from the first [mark] until the latter [one] heals.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:13:1.hebrew: ומת - הצורם. מהו לקנוס בנו אחריו — שלא יאכל מאותו בכור עולמית:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:13:1.english: And dies - The one who slit [the ear]. What is [the law regarding whether] to penalize his son after him — that he may not eat from that firstborn forever?

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:14:1.hebrew: אם תימצי לומר - במסכת גיטין, דהמוכר עבדו לעובד כוכבים, דקיימא לן: קונסין אותו לפדותו עד עשרה בדמיו, ומיבעיא לן התם: אם מת המוכר, מהו לקנוס בנו אחריו? אם תימצי לומר ולמיפשט בההיא דקונסין — התם דינא הוא, דכל יומא מפקע ליה ממצות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:14:1.english: If you say - [This refers to] Tractate Gittin, where [in the case of] one who sells his slave to a gentile, we maintain that we penalize him [by requiring him] to redeem him up to ten times his value, and it was raised as a dilemma for us there: If the seller dies, what is [the ruling regarding] penalizing his son after him? If you say and resolve in that [case] that we penalize [the son] — there it is justified, as each day [the master] prevents him from [performing] mitzvot.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:15:1.hebrew: ואם תימצי לומר - הא דאמרינן במ"ק (דף יב:): המכוין מלאכתו במועד — דמניח כרמו לבצור, ואומר: "במועד אבצירנה, שהרי דבר האבוד הוא, והתירוהו חכמים במועד" — תאבד ולא יבצרנה, הואיל ולכך נתכוין. ומיבעיא לן התם: אם מת קודם המועד, מהו לקנוס בנו אחריו, ולא יבצרנה במועד? ואם תימצי לומר: התם הוא דלא קנסינן לבנו, דהא לא עביד אביו איסורא, דהא מת קודם המועד:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:15:1.english: And if you say - [Regarding] that which we say in Moed Katan (daf 12b): [With regard to] "one who deliberately plans his labor for the Festival" — where he leaves his vineyard to harvest and says, "I will harvest it during the Festival, for it is an irretrievable loss, and the Sages permitted [such labor] during the Festival" — "it shall be lost" and he may not harvest it, since this was his intent. And we raised a dilemma there: If he died before the Festival, what is [the law as to whether] to penalize his son after him, such that he may not harvest it during the Festival? And if you say [in resolution]: It is [only] there that we do not penalize his son, because his father did not perform a prohibited act, as he died before the Festival.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:16:1.hebrew: אבל הכא - עבד איסורא, דמטיל מום בקדשים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:16:1.english: But here - He committed a transgression, as he inflicted a blemish upon consecrated [animals].

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:1.hebrew: שנתקווצה - שנטל קוציה ממנה, שהיו תלושין ומפוזרין בה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:1.english: Whose thorns were removed - That one removed its thorns from it, which were detached and scattered in it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:2.hebrew: תזרע למוצאי שביעית - דליכא למיקנס מידי, דהא לא עבד בשביעית עבודה חשובה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:2.english: [It] may be sown at the conclusion of the Sabbatical [Year] - For there is nothing to penalize [him for], as he did not perform significant labor during the Sabbatical [Year].

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:3.hebrew: ניטייבה - נזדבלה ע"י עגלות ומשואות של זבל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:3.english: It had been improved - It was fertilized by means of wagons and loads of manure.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:4.hebrew: נידיירה - על ידי דיר בהמות, שמעמידין ומשכיבין אותה חדש או חדשים, כדי לזבלה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:4.english: It had been enclosed - By means of an animal pen, where they keep [the animals] standing and lying down for a month or two months, in order to fertilize it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:5.hebrew: לא תזרע - דקנסינן, דעבד עבודה חשובה בשביעית:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:17:5.english: It may not be sown - For we penalize [him], as he performed significant labor during the Sabbatical [Year].

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:1:1.english: And it was excised - That he did not intend to excise it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:1:2.english: When another leprous mark develops on him - For behold, he is presently ritually impure and afflicted.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:1:3.hebrew: יטהר - מן הראשונה, והולכין אחר זו. ואם ירפא מזו — טהור מכולם, דאיגלאי מילתא דאי (נמי) הוי קמייתא, מיתסי נמי כי האי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:1:3.english: He will become ritually pure - From the first [mark]; and we follow this [new one]. And if he is healed from this [one], he is ritually pure from all of them, for the matter is revealed that if the first [mark] had [also] been [present], it too would have healed like this one.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:2:1.hebrew: עד שתפרח בכולו - נגע האחרון. וליכא למיחש למידי, דהא אי הוה ביה קמא, השתא נמי הוה טהור, כדכתיב (ויקרא י״ג:י״ב) וכסתה הצרעת את כל עור הנגע וגו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:2:1.english: Until it spreads over all of him - [Meaning,] the latter affliction. And there is nothing to be concerned about, for even if the first [affliction] were [still] on him, he would also be pure now, as it is written (Leviticus 13:12): “And the leprosy cover all the skin of the affliction, etc.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:2:2.hebrew: או עד שתתמעט בהרתו - הראשונה מכגריס קודם שקצצה. אבל אי בשעה שקצצה הוה ביה שיעור נגע — אין לו טהרה עולמית, דקנסינן ליה לעולם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:2:2.english: Or until his baheret diminishes - The first [baheret had shrunk to less] than a split bean before he cut it off. But if at the time he cut it off there was the requisite measure of a leprous mark in it, he never attains ritual purity, for we penalize him forever.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:4:1.hebrew: בממונו אתי ליה למיעבד - ממה נפשך, דסבר: אטיל בו מום; ואם יתירוהו לי בכך — הרי נשכרתי, ואם לאו — מה הפסדתי? אם אמתין למום אחר, בלא"ה נמי הייתי ממתין עד שיפול מום. הלכך, קנסינן ליה אפי' יפול בו מום אחר, כי היכי דלא ליתי וליעביד:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:4:1.english: With regard to his property, he might come to do [so] - Either way, for he reasons: I will inflict a blemish upon it; and if they permit it to me on account of that, behold, I have gained; and if not, what have I lost? If I [must] wait for another blemish, even without this I would also have waited until a blemish befell [it]. Therefore, we penalize him even if another blemish falls upon it, so that he will not come to do [so].

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:4:2.hebrew: בגופו מי איכא למימר - דמנחי' לספיקא וליקוץ, אי לא קנסינן ליה לעולם? הא ודאי לא עביד, דחייש: שמא נגע אחר לא יוולד לו לעולם, ולא אטהר לעולם. ואפי' אם יוולד — מה אהני לו בקציצה? הרי הוא נגוע כבתחלה! מוטב לו להניח את זה, שמא ירפא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:4:2.english: With regard to his body, is there [reason] to say - that he would leave [the matter] in doubt and cut [it off], if we do not penalize him forever? This he certainly would not do, for he fears: Perhaps another affliction will never appear on him, and [he thinks,] "I will never become pure!" And even if [another mark] will appear — what did cutting [it off] benefit him? Behold, he is afflicted as at first! It is better for him to leave this [mark], lest it heal.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:7:1.hebrew: בהאי מומא - לא מישתרי ליה, עד שיוולד לו אחר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:7:1.english: By means of this blemish - It will not become permitted to him until another [blemish] develops on it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:7:2.hebrew: בהאי קציצה - וכיון דהך קציצה אינה מועלת לטהרו, נמצא טמא עולמית, דחשבינן לנגע כמאן דאיתיה — דמי יימר דאי הוה ביה, הוה מיתסי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:7:2.english: With this excision - And since this excision is not effective in purifying him, he turns out to be impure forever, for we consider the affliction as though it is [still] present — as who is to say that if it were [still] on him, it would heal?

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:8:1.hebrew: יטהר תנן - דמשמע: מיד כשיוולד בו נגע אחר, יטהר מן הראשונה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:8:1.english: Did we learn: “He will become ritually pure” - Which implies that immediately when another [leprous] mark appears on him, he becomes ritually pure from the first [mark].

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:8:2.hebrew: או ויטהר תנן - דמשמע: כשיוולד נגע אחר ויטהר ממנו — מן האחרון — אז יטהר מן הראשון:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:8:2.english: Or did we learn: “And he will become pure” - Which implies that when another mark appears and he becomes pure from it — from the latter one — then he will become pure from the first.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:9:1.english: For a bridegroom upon whom a leprous mark appeared - That the latter mark appeared on him during the days of [his] wedding.

Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:9:2.hebrew: למאי נפקא מינה - הא א"נ יטהר תנן — הא טמא הוא מן האחרון עד שתרפא, (ממה נפשך) וממה נפשך טומאה שייכא ביה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 34b:9:2.english: What is the practical difference - For even if we learned "he shall become pure," behold, he is impure on account of the latter [mark] until it heals, and in either case ritual impurity applies to him.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:11:1.hebrew: מקמייתא טהר לי' לבתרייתא נטרי' ליה ז' ימי המשתה - וא"ת: והא בעי תגלחת וצפרים, ואסור בתשמיש המטה כל ימי ספורו? וי"ל: כגון שלא היה אלא מצורע מוסגר. א"נ, אפילו מוחלט — נהי דכי קצץ טמא מדרבנן, מ"מ שרי לעשות תגלחת וצפרים ולמנות ימי ספורו וליטהר מן התורה. ומיהו כפרתו א"א להביא, דאינו יכול להכניס ידיו לבהונות כל זמן דטמא מדרבנן, כדאמר (פסחים דף צב.): "אע"פ שאין טבול יום אחר נכנס, זה נכנס" — דלא התירו אלא משום פסח:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:11:1.english: "From the first [mark] he has become pure; for the latter [mark] we wait for him the seven days of the feast" - And if you say: But doesn't he require shaving and birds, and he is forbidden marital relations throughout the days of his counting? And one can say: For example, where he was only a quarantined leper. Alternatively, even [if he was] a certified [leper]: Granted that when he excised [the mark] he is ritually impure by rabbinic decree, nevertheless, it is permitted [for him] to perform shaving and [bring] birds, to count the days of his counting, and to become pure by Torah law. However, it is impossible to bring his atonement [offerings], because he cannot insert his hands for [the application of blood and oil to] his thumbs [and big toes] as long as he is ritually impure by rabbinic decree, as [the Gemara] says (Pesachim 92a): "Although another tevul yom may not enter, this one enters" — for they permitted [this entry] only for the sake of the Paschal offering.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:13:1.hebrew: בעא מיניה ר' ירמיה מר' זירא צורם אוזן בכור ומת מהו שיקנסו בנו אחריו - בפרק השולח (גיטין מד.) נקט תחלה הבעיא דמוכר עבדו, ובמו"ק בפרק מי שהפך (מועד קטן דף יב:) נקט בכוון מלאכתו, ובכל דוכתי עביד אם תימצי לומר מאידך, ואכולהו פשיט: "תניתוה משדה שנתקווצה". ואומר רבי דשלשתם שאל בבת אחת, והש"ס קבע כל אחת במקומה כפי מה ששייכא. ויש ספרים שכתוב במ"ק (שם): "בעא מיניה רבא מר"נ", אבל ברוב הספרים גרסינן: "ר' ירמיה מרבי זירא", כמו כאן ובגיטין:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:13:1.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised a dilemma before Rabbi Zeira: [In the case of] one who slits the ear of a firstborn and dies, what is [the halakha as to whether] they penalize his son after him? - In the chapter [entitled] HaSholeiach (Gittin 44a), [the Gemara] presents the dilemma of one who sells his slave first; and in Moed Katan, in the chapter [entitled] Mi SheHafakh (Moed Katan 12b), it presents [the dilemma of] one who intentionally scheduled his labor [for the intermediate days of a Festival]; and in each place, it constructs an "if you want to say" [argument] from the other [cases]; and for all of them, it resolves [the dilemma]: "You have learned it [from the mishna regarding] a field that was cleared of thorns." And the Rabbi says that he asked all three of them at one time, and the Talmud positioned each one in its [respective] place according to where it belongs. And there are books in which it is written in Moed Katan (ibid.): "Rava raised a dilemma before Rav Nachman"; however, in most books the reading is: "Rabbi Yirmeya [raised a dilemma] before Rabbi Zeira," as [is the reading] here and in Gittin.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:14:1.hebrew: אם תמצא לומר מוכר עבדו לעובדי כוכבים ומת קנסו בנו אחריו דכל יומא מפקע ליה ממצות - אכתי המ"ל: דאפילו תימצי לומר התם לא קנסו, (דדלמא) הכא קנסו משום דאיכא איסורא דאורייתא — דכי האי גוונא איכא בפ' השולח גבי בעיא דמוכר עבדו, ובמ"ק גבי בעיא דכוון מלאכתו במועד, דקאמר: "אם תימצי לומר בצורם קנסו משום דאיכא אסורא דאורייתא". ובגיטין נמי הוה מצי למינקט: אם תימצי לומר לא קנסו, הכא קנסו משום הפקעת מצות דכל יומא ויומא, (כמו) בעבד. ובמ"ק נמי נקט חד טעמא בצורם וטעמא אחרינא במוכר עבדו, והוה מצי למימר חד טעמא בתרוייהו: דאם תימצי לומר בצורם ובמוכר דקנסוה משום דעבדיה לאיסורא, אבל כוון מלאכתו לא עבד לאיסורא:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:14:1.english: "If you say [in the case of] one who sells his slave to gentiles and dies, they penalized his son after him, because every day he prevents him from mitzvot" - Still, [the Gemara] could have said: Even if you say that there [in the case of selling a slave] they did not penalize [his son], [perhaps] here [in the case of slitting the ear of a firstborn] they penalized [him] because there is a Torah prohibition — for a case like this exists in the chapter [entitled] HaSholei'ach (Gittin 44a) regarding the dilemma of one who sells his slave, and in Moed Katan (13a) regarding the dilemma of one who planned his labor on the intermediate days of the Festival, where [the Gemara] states: "If you say that in [the case of] one who slits [the ear of a firstborn] they penalized [his son], because there is a Torah prohibition." And in Gittin as well, [the Gemara] could have formulated: "If you say [that in the case of one who slits the ear of a firstborn] they did not penalize [his son], here [in the case of selling a slave] they penalized [him] because of the prevention of mitzvot each and every day, [as occurs] with a slave." And in Moed Katan as well, [the Gemara] stated one reason regarding one who slits [the ear of a firstborn] and another reason regarding one who sells his slave, whereas it could have stated a single reason for both of them: that "If you say that in [both the case of] one who slits and [the case of] one who sells [a slave] they penalized [his son], [that is] because he performed a prohibited act; but [one who] planned his labor did not perform a prohibited act."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:17:1.hebrew: שנתקווצה - פי' בקונט': שנטל קוצים ממנה שהיו תלושין ומפוזרין בה. והדין עמו, דא"א לומר בקוצים שהיו מחוברים — דא"כ לא תזרע, דאיכא איסורא דאורייתא בנטילתם שמייפה את הקרקע, כדאמר שבת פרק הבונה (שבת דף קג.) גבי [התולש עולשין והמזרד זרדים]: דבארעא דיליה חייב (בכל דיליה חייב) בכל שהוא משום דאיכא יפוי הקרקע, דאפי' מתכוין לצורך דבר אחר; וה"נ איכא יפוי קרקע כשתולש קוצים לחורשה לזריעה. וכן משמע בירושלמי על המשנה: "תמן אסורים כשנטלו קוציה", משמע דמוקי לה בתלושין:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:17:1.english: "Whose thorns were removed" - Rashi explained in the commentary that he removed thorns from it that were detached and scattered in it. And he is correct, for it is impossible to say [that the Mishnah is referring] to thorns that were attached [to the ground] — because if so, [the field] would not be sown, as there is a Torah prohibition in removing them, since it improves the land; as [the Gemara] says in Shabbat, chapter HaBoneh (Shabbat 103a), regarding [the Mishnah: "One who plucks endives and one who prunes twigs"]: that on his own land he is liable (on anything of his, he is liable) for any amount because there is improvement of the land, even if he intends for another purpose; and here too, there is improvement of the land when he plucks thorns to plow it for sowing. And so it is implied in the Yerushalmi on the Mishnah: "There they are prohibited when its thorns were removed," which implies that it establishes [the Mishnah as referring] to detached [thorns].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:17:2.hebrew: ניטייבה - בירושלמי מפרש: איזהו טיוב? כל העם פעם אחת חורשין, והוא חורש שתי פעמים:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:17:2.english: "It had been improved" - In the Yerushalmi it explains: What is improvement? All the people plow once, but he plows twice.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:17:3.hebrew: הטיבה ומת בנו זורעה - אם האי טיוב מדרבנן, קשה: היכי פשיט צורם אוזן בכור דאורייתא? ואם הוא נמי דאורייתא, קשה בגיטין (דף מד:) דפשיט מיניה גבי עבד (עברי), לימא: שאני הכא דחמיר משום דמפקע ליה ממצות? וי"ל: דקסבר שראוי להחמיר בשביעית יותר מכולם, כדאמר בקדושין (דף כ.): "כמה קשה אבקה של שביעית":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:17:3.english: [If he] improved it and died, his son may sow it - If this improvement [of the field] is Rabbinic, it is difficult: How does [the Gemara] resolve [the dilemma regarding] one who slits the ear of a firstborn, which is [prohibited by] Torah law? And if it is also [prohibited by] Torah law, it is difficult in Gittin (44b), where [the Gemara] resolves from it [the dilemma] regarding a slave (Hebrew) — let us say: Here it is different, for it is more severe, because he removes him from [the observance of] mitzvot? And one can say that he maintains that it is fitting to be more stringent regarding the Sabbatical Year than all of them, as [the Gemara] says in Kiddushin (20a): "How severe is the dust of the Sabbatical Year!"

Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:2:1.hebrew: עד שתפרח בכולו - בכל הספרים [כתוב]: "עד שתתמעט בהרתו מכגריס", אבל במס' נגעים ליתיה, כדפי' בקונט'. ואומר רבי: דאי גרסינן לי', ה"פ — שאם קצצה ונעשה בכגריס, ומה ששייר נתרפא מקצתו מעצמו, שאפי' היה בו מה שנקצצה, לא היה בו כגריס:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 34b:2:1.english: "Until it spreads over his entire [body]" - In all the books [it is written]: "Until his baheret diminishes to less than [the size of] a split bean," but in Tractate Negaim it is not [present], as explained in the Kuntres. And the Rabbi says: If we read it, this is its explanation — that if he excised [part of] it and it became [the size of] a split bean, and what remained partially healed on its own, such that even if what was excised were [still] in it, there would not be [the size of] a split bean in it.
